title: Package a Java service with Maven
summary: Fix a POM so it compiles for Java 21 and keeps JUnit on the test classpath.

scenario.briefing: A service POM still targets Java 11 and has no test dependency. Update the build so mvn verify compiles for Java 21 and runs JUnit tests without shipping them.

objectives.description: Set the Java release and test dependency in the POM.
Choose the Maven command that verifies the build.
Explain Maven, Gradle, and dependency scope accurately.

hints: Read the properties and dependencies sections of the POM.
Use mvn verify to run the full lifecycle.

misconceptions.description: Leaving the compiler release at Java 11.
misconceptions.testDescription: The compiler release is fixed to Java 21.
misconceptions.feedback: The release property controls the bytecode target. Set it to 21 so the build matches the service runtime.

misconceptions.description: Using the default scope for a test library.
misconceptions.feedback: JUnit should use test scope so it is available to tests and excluded from the production artifact.

misconceptions.description: Running only compile when tests and packaging matter.
misconceptions.feedback: mvn compile stops before tests and packaging. mvn verify runs the full lifecycle.

sections.title: Maven describes a build in a POM
sections.body: pom.xml declares the project coordinates, Java release, dependencies, and plugins. The lifecycle runs validate, compile, test, package, and verify in order. mvn verify runs the full sequence and is the usual local check before a commit.

sections.title: Dependency scope limits availability
sections.body: Compile-scope dependencies are available to production code. Test-scope dependencies such as JUnit are available only to tests and are not packaged into the artifact. Keeping test libraries out of production reduces the attack surface and the artifact size.

sections.title: Gradle solves the same problem differently
sections.body: Gradle uses a build script and a task graph instead of a fixed lifecycle. Both Maven and Gradle can compile, test, and package Java. The Maven Wrapper or the Gradle Wrapper pins the build tool version so a repository builds the same way on every machine.

steps.title: Fix the project POM
steps.prompt: Edit pom.xml. Target Java 21, set the project version to 1.0.0, and add JUnit Jupiter with test scope.

files.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
  <groupId>com.praxbit</groupId>
  <artifactId>campus-service</artifactId>
  <version>0.0.0</version>
  <properties>
    <maven.compiler.release>11</maven.compiler.release>
  </properties>
  <!-- TODO: add the JUnit test dependency -->
</project>

tests.description: The compiler release is fixed to Java 21.
JUnit is available to tests only.
The project version is no longer a placeholder.

hints: JUnit Jupiter belongs in a dependencies block.
Test libraries use the test scope.
Replace the placeholder version and remove the TODO.

localVerification.description: Run the Maven lifecycle through tests and packaging.

steps.title: Choose the verification command
steps.prompt: A change touches production code and tests. Which Maven command runs the full lifecycle through verification?

quiz.explanation: mvn verify runs compile, test, package, and verification checks. compile stops early, skipping tests hides failures, and running the jar does not rebuild.

hints: The command should run tests and packaging.
Package alone can still skip checks.
The verify phase is the last lifecycle phase.

steps.title: Build lifecycle and scope

statements.label: The Maven lifecycle runs compile, test, package, and verify in order.
Test-scope dependencies are packaged into production artifacts.
The Maven Wrapper pins the Maven version for a repository.
Gradle uses a build script and can also run the same tests.

steps.explanation: Maven orders build work by lifecycle phase. Test scope keeps test libraries out of the artifact, and wrappers make builds reproducible.
hints: Both Maven and Gradle can compile and test Java.

accessibility.summary: The editor and checks are keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure; they do not compile or run the language.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and the results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the first mismatch or missing source fragment.
